questions.question: Explain the impact of festivals on pilgrimage tourism.
questions.solution_html:
• Increased VisitationFestivals create fixed dates for mass gatherings, generating huge, predictable surges in
  • pilgrim arrivals.
  • Economic Boost They drive massive revenue for local economies through spending on accommodation
  • transport, food, and religious offerings.
  • Infrastructure Development Festivals necessitate and spur the building or upgrading of essential amenities
  • (roads, sanitation, temporary housing, crowd management).
  • Social Cohesion They enhance the feeling of community and shared faith among pilgrims, strengthening the
  • spiritual and social bond of the site.
  • Cultural Promotion Festivals integrate local arts, music, and rituals into the pilgrimage, promoting the unique
  • cultural heritage of the destination to a wider audience.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: cultural heritage of the destination to a wider audience.

questions.question: Analyze economic benefits of diverse tourism products in India.
questions.solution_html:
• Diversified Foreign Exchange Earnings: By offering products like Medical Tourism, Heritage Tourism
  • and Adventure Tourism, India can attract high-spending international visitors throughout the year
  • ensuring a steady and varied inflow of foreign currency.
  • Wider Employment Generation: Diverse products create specialized jobs across various sectors (e.g.
  • Doctors for Medical Tourism, Guides for Heritage sites, trainers for Adventure sports), increasing
  • overall employment volume and skill diversity in both urban and rural areas.
  • Reduced Regional Disparities: The focus on niche products (like Eco-Tourism and Wellness) drives
  • investment and tourist traffic to previously underserved regions and rural areas (e.g., homestays
  • in the Northeast or Ayurveda centers in Kerala), ensuring more equitable economic growth across
  • the country.
  • Enhanced Multiplier Effect: Diversification stimulates growth in related industries (forward and backward
  • linkages). For instance, Wellness Tourism boosts demand for local organic products and Ayurvedic
  • equipment, multiplying the initial tourist spending across multiple local supply chains and
  • MSMEs.
  • Year-Round Revenue Stability: Relying on a mix of products (e.g., beaches in winter, mountains in
  • summer, and medical/heritage year-round) reduces the impact of seasonality, providing the sector
  • with a more stable and predictable revenue stream regardless of weather or regional fluctuations.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: with a more stable and predictable revenue stream regardless of weather or regional fluctuations.

questions.question: Analyse the impact of performing arts on cultural identity and tourism.
questions.solution_html:
• Reinforces Cultural Identity: Performing arts act as a living archive, passing down indigenous
  • stories, customs, and philosophies across generations. This continuous tradition strengthens the sense of
  • identity and authenticity for the local community.
  • Creates Unique Tourist Attractions: Performances (such as Kathakali in Kerala or the Ghoomar in
  • Rajasthan) transform a simple location into a dynamic cultural product. They offer tourists a unique
  • experiential reason to visit that cannot be found elsewhere.
  • Preserves Intangible Heritage: Tourism demand for authentic performances provides an economic
  • incentive to maintain traditional art forms, saving them from obsolescence and providing livelihoods for
  • artists who are keepers of the culture.
  • Enhances Destination Branding: A distinct performing art form (e.g., Bhangra for Punjab or
  • Mohiniyattam for Kerala) becomes a powerful visual symbol and marketing tool, giving the destination a
  • recognizable and memorable cultural brand identity on the global stage.
  • Encourages Deep Cultural Exchange: Watching a traditional performance moves tourists beyond
  • simple sightseeing. It fosters emotional connection, increases cultural understanding, and encourages
  • visitors to seek out further interaction, transforming them from passive consumers into appreciative
  • guests.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Compare North and South Indian culinary traditions in tourism context.
questions.solution_html:
• North Indian cuisine attracts tourists with its rich, creamy, and wheat-based dishes (like naan, butter
  • chicken, and tandoori), reflecting Mughal influence and suiting colder climates.
  • Conversely, South Indian cuisine appeals to travelers seeking lighter, tangier, and often healthier
  • options that are predominantly rice-based, featuring coconut, curry leaves, and fermentation (like
  • idli, dosa, and sambar).
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Analyze the importance of inter-governmental coordination (Central, State, and local bodies) in the growth and management of Indian tourism.
questions.solution_html:
• Unified Policy and Standards: Central bodies set national standards and marketing strategies
  • (e.g., Incredible India), which require State and local bodies to implement them uniformly
  • ensuring a consistent, high-quality tourist experience across all regions.
  • Infrastructure Synergy: Major projects like national highways, airport development (Central)
  • and last-mile connectivity/local roads (State/Local) require joint planning and funding to ensure
  • tourists can access destinations efficiently from national entry points.
  • Safety and Security: Effective security and disaster management protocols must be
  • coordinated between Central agencies (intelligence), State police, and local law enforcement
  • guaranteeing tourist safety and confidence in the destination.
  • Resource Mobilization: Sharing of financial resources (Central grants like PRASAD or
  • SWADESH) and technical expertise between the three tiers allows for the optimal utilization of
  • funds to develop major projects that no single body could undertake alone.
  • Regulation and Licensing: Clear demarcation of licensing authority and environmental
  • oversight among the three tiers prevents bureaucratic hurdles and conflicts, enabling faster
  • approval for private investments while maintaining sustainable practices.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
questions.final_answer: approval for private investments while maintaining sustainable practices.

questions.question: Discuss the role of pilgrimage tourism in India’s tourism industry, highlighting major destinations of different religions
questions.solution_html:
• Massive Economic Contribution: Pilgrimage sites generate vast and consistent revenue through
  • donations, local services (food, flowers, souvenirs), and transportation, creating millions of jobs and
  • contributing significantly to the national GDP.
  • Essential Infrastructure Driver: The constant influx of large crowds necessitates major government
  • investment in infrastructure projects (roads, rail links, airports, sanitation) under schemes like PRASAD
  • directly benefiting both pilgrims and the local population.
  • National and Social Integration: Pilgrimage fosters a sense of unity by drawing domestic and
  • international visitors from all socio-economic backgrounds and regions to shared sacred spaces
  • promoting national cohesion and inter-cultural understanding.
  • Preservation of Heritage: The financial viability driven by pilgrims ensures the maintenance, protection
  • and restoration of ancient temples, mosques, churches, and stupas, safeguarding India's diverse
  • architectural and religious heritage.
  • Major Multi-Religious Destinations: India's strength lies in its diverse destinations
  • Hindu: Varanasi (Kashi Vishwanath), Tirupati (Andhra Pradesh), Char Dham (Badrinath, Puri
  • Rameshwaram, Dwarka).
  • Sikh: Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib), Amritsar.
  • Islamic: Ajmer Sharif Dargah (Rajasthan), Haji Ali Dargah (Mumbai).
  • Buddhist: Bodh Gaya (Bihar), Sarnath (Uttar Pradesh).
  • Christian: Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health (Velankanni, Tamil Nadu), St. Thomas Syro-Malabar
  • Church (Malayattoor, Kerala).
